copy.name: How to calculate hours worked on a time card
copy.blurb: Enter start, end and unpaid break for each shift. 09:00–17:30 with 30 minutes off is 8 hours, five days is 40, and a Saturday 09:00–14:00 adds 5 hours of overtime: 950.00 at 20 an hour with 1.5× overtime.
copy.title: How to calculate hours worked on a time card
copy.lead: You have a week of clock-in and clock-out times and want the hours, the overtime and the pay. You will enter each shift once and read the totals. Five shifts of 09:00–17:30 with a 30-minute break are 40 hours; a Saturday morning on top makes 45, with 5 hours of overtime. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: Hours per shift, the week's total in hours:minutes and decimal hours, regular and overtime hours, and gross pay if you entered a rate.
copy.note: Open the time card calculator with your shift times at hand. Enter unpaid breaks only; paid breaks count as work. Overtime rules differ by country and contract, so set the threshold and multiplier to match yours. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: For each day you need the clock-in time, the clock-out time and the unpaid break in minutes. One shift = end − start − break: 09:00 to 17:30 is 8 hours 30 minutes, minus 30 minutes is 8 hours.
copy.s2t: Open Time card calculator on cv.cm
copy.s2b: Five shifts of 09:00–17:30 with 30-minute breaks are filled: 40:00 hours. Each row shows its hours on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Change the start, end and break per row. Add shift adds a sixth day; × removes a row. A row marked ! has a missing time or a break longer than the shift.
copy.s4b: If the end time is earlier than the start, the shift runs past midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours and shows a ☾. Do not split it into two days.
copy.s5b: Add Saturday 09:00–14:00 with no break: total 45:00, regular 40:00, overtime 5:00. With a rate of 20 and the default 1.5×, gross pay is 800 + 150 = 950.00.
copy.s6t: Convert to decimal hours and copy
copy.s6b: Payroll often wants decimal hours: divide minutes by 60, so 7:45 is 7.75. The totals show both forms. Copy puts them on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: One shift = end − start − unpaid break: 09:00–17:30 minus 30 minutes is 8 hours.
copy.diagram2: 45 hours in a week with a 40-hour threshold: 40 regular + 5 overtime at 1.5×.

faq.q1: Can I calculate hours worked free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm adds the shifts in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q2: How many hours is 9 to 5:30 with a 30-minute break?
faq.a2: 8 hours. 8.5 hours on the clock minus the unpaid break.
faq.q3: How do I convert 7 hours 45 minutes to decimal?
faq.a3: Divide the minutes by 60: 45 ÷ 60 = 0.75, so 7.75 hours.
faq.a4: Yes. An end time before the start runs past midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours.
faq.q5: Is the overtime rule right for my job?
faq.a5: The default is over 40 hours a week at 1.5×. Some places count daily overtime or use 2×; set the threshold and multiplier to your rules.

copy.name: How to calculate the electricity cost of an appliance
copy.blurb: Watts × hours ÷ 1000 = kWh; kWh × your price = cost. A 1000 W air conditioner for 8 hours a day for 30 days uses 240 kWh: 36.00 at 0.15 a kWh, 438.00 a year.
copy.title: How to calculate the electricity cost of an appliance
copy.lead: You want to know what an appliance adds to the bill. You will read its watts, estimate how long it runs and multiply by your price per kWh. A 1000 W air conditioner running 8 hours a day for a month uses 240 kWh; at 0.15 that is 36.00. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: Cost for the period, energy in kWh, cost and kWh per day, and cost per year, in whatever currency you type.
copy.note: Open the electricity cost calculator with the appliance label and your latest bill at hand. Fridges and air conditioners cycle on and off, so their real use is lower than the label. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: Energy in kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Cost = kWh × price per kWh. A 1000 W heater running one hour uses exactly 1 kWh.
copy.s2t: Open Electricity cost calculator on cv.cm
copy.s2b: A 1000 W air conditioner, 8 hours a day, 30 days at 0.15 per kWh is filled. The cost sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Pick a preset or type the watts from the label or manual. If the label gives amps, multiply by the voltage: 5 A × 220 V = 1100 W.
copy.s4b: Type the hours a day it runs and the number of days. Take the price per kWh from your bill: energy charge ÷ kWh used. For several identical devices set How many.
copy.s5b: The air conditioner: 240 kWh, 36.00 for the month, 1.20 a day, 438.00 a year. A 10 W LED bulb for 5 hours a day uses 1.5 kWh a month: 0.30 at 0.20 a kWh.
copy.s6t: Account for cycling and standby, then copy
copy.s6b: A 150 W fridge on 24 hours shows 3.6 kWh a day, but the compressor runs about a third of the time, so expect nearer 1.2. Standby of a few watts all year adds up to tens of kWh. Copy puts the numbers on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000; cost = kWh × price per kWh.
copy.diagram2: 1000 W × 8 h × 30 days = 240 kWh; at 0.15 that is 36.00 a month.

faq.q1: Can I calculate appliance electricity cost free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q2: How much does a 1000 W appliance cost per hour?
faq.a2: It uses 1 kWh an hour, so the cost equals your price per kWh, for example 0.15.
faq.q3: How do I convert amps to watts?
faq.a3: Multiply amps by volts: 5 A at 220 V is 1100 W, at 120 V it is 600 W.
faq.q4: Why is my fridge's real use lower?
faq.a4: The compressor runs only part of the time, often about a third, so the label watts overstate daily use.
faq.a5: Whatever you type for the price. The result is in the same currency.

copy.name: How to find your fertile window and ovulation day
copy.blurb: Ovulation is about 14 days before the next period. A period starting 1 January with a 28-day cycle gives ovulation on 15 January, a fertile window of 10–16 January and the next period on 29 January.
copy.title: How to find your fertile window and ovulation day
copy.lead: You know when your last period started and roughly how long your cycle is. You will find the likely ovulation day, the six-day fertile window and the next period for the next three cycles. With a 1 January start and 28 days, ovulation falls on 15 January. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: For each of the next three cycles: the fertile window, the likely ovulation day and the next period.
copy.note: Open the ovulation calculator with your period dates at hand. Use the average of your last few cycles. It is an estimate, not contraception or medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: The time from ovulation to the next period, the luteal phase, is about 14 days for most people. The part before ovulation is what varies, so ovulation = next period − 14 days.
copy.s2b: A sample last period and a 28-day cycle are filled. Three cycles sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type the first day of your last period, the first day of bleeding. For 1 January with 28 days, the next period is 29 January.
copy.s4b: Count from the first day of one period to the day before the next and average a few cycles. A 32-day cycle moves ovulation from 15 January to 19 January.
copy.s5b: The window is the five days before ovulation and the day after: 10–16 January. Sperm can live up to five days and the egg about one, so these six days carry the highest chance.
copy.s6t: Treat it as an estimate, then copy
copy.s6b: Cycles shift by a few days from month to month, and calendar estimates miss many ovulations. Ovulation test strips give a better signal. Copy puts the dates on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Ovulation ≈ next period − 14 days; the fertile window runs from 5 days before to 1 day after.
copy.diagram2: Period 1 January, 28 days: fertile 10–16 January, ovulation 15 January, next period 29 January.

faq.q1: Can I calculate my ovulation day free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm estimates it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
faq.q2: When do I ovulate with a 28-day cycle?
faq.a2: Around day 14, counting the first day of your period as day 1.
faq.q3: How long is the fertile window?
faq.a3: About six days: the five days before ovulation and the day after.
faq.q4: Can I use this to avoid pregnancy?
faq.a4: No. Calendar estimates are not reliable contraception. Use a proper method and ask a doctor.
faq.q5: My cycle is irregular. What should I enter?
faq.a5: The average of your last six cycles. Irregular cycles make the estimate less accurate; ovulation tests help.

copy.name: How to calculate your macros in grams
copy.blurb: Split a calorie target into protein, fat and carbs. Grams = calories × share ÷ 4 for protein and carbs, ÷ 9 for fat. 2500 kcal at 30/30/40 is 188 g protein, 83 g fat and 250 g carbs.
copy.title: How to calculate your macros in grams
copy.lead: You know roughly how many calories you need and want to turn that into grams on a food label. You will pick a goal and a split and read protein, fat and carbohydrate in grams. 2500 kcal with a balanced 30/30/40 split is 188 g protein, 83 g fat and 250 g carbs. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: A daily calorie target and grams of protein, fat and carbohydrate, plus protein per kg if you entered your weight.
copy.note: Open the macro calculator with your maintenance calories at hand; the TDEE calculator estimates them. A starting point for healthy adults, not medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: Protein and carbohydrate have 4 kcal per gram, fat has 9. So grams = calories for that macro ÷ 4 or ÷ 9. 750 kcal of protein is 187.5 g.
copy.s2b: 2500 kcal, maintain weight and a balanced split are set. The grams sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type your maintenance calories. Lose weight subtracts 500 kcal; gain adds 300. 2500 maintenance becomes 2000 to lose weight.
copy.s4b: Balanced is 30/30/40 (protein/fat/carbs %), high protein 40/30/30, low carb 35/45/20. 2000 kcal high protein is 200 g protein, 67 g fat and 150 g carbs.
copy.s5b: Type your weight. 200 g at 70 kg is 2.9 g per kg; active adults often aim for 1.6–2.2. Pick a lower-protein split if yours is far above that.
copy.s6t: Turn grams into meals, then copy
copy.s6b: Divide by the number of meals: 200 g protein over four meals is 50 g each. Copy puts the target and grams on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Grams = calories × share ÷ 4 for protein and carbs, ÷ 9 for fat.
copy.diagram2: 2500 kcal at 30/30/40: 188 g protein, 83 g fat, 250 g carbs.

faq.q1: Can I calculate macros free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q2: How many grams of protein is 30% of 2000 kcal?
faq.a3: A gram of fat has 9 kcal; protein and carbohydrate have 4.
faq.a4: Balanced suits most people. High protein helps keep muscle while losing weight; low carb suits people who prefer fewer carbs.
faq.q5: Where do I get my calories?
faq.a5: From the TDEE calculator, which estimates maintenance calories from age, size and activity.

copy.name: How to calculate calories burned during exercise
copy.blurb: Calories = MET × body weight in kg × hours. 30 minutes at 70 kg: running at 10 km/h about 343 kcal, jumping rope 413, cycling 280, swimming 203, yoga 88.
copy.title: How to calculate calories burned during exercise
copy.lead: You want to know what a workout burns. You will pick an activity, enter your weight and minutes, and read the calories from its MET value. 30 minutes of running at 10 km/h at 70 kg burns about 343 kcal. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: Calories burned, calories per minute, the MET value, a fat equivalent and the same minutes for 15 other activities.
copy.note: Open the calories burned calculator after the workout or while planning it. MET values are averages; your real burn can differ by 20% or more. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: One MET is the energy you use sitting still, about 1 kcal per kg per hour. Running at 10 km/h is 9.8 MET, nearly ten times rest. Calories = MET × kg × hours.
copy.s2t: Open Calories burned calculator on cv.cm
copy.s2b: Brisk walking, 70 kg and 30 minutes are set. The result and a comparison list sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type your weight in kg or switch to lb, and the minutes. Heavier people burn more for the same activity, because the formula scales with weight.
copy.s4b: Choose from 16 activities with MET values from the 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities. Running at 10 km/h for 30 minutes at 70 kg: 9.8 × 70 × 0.5 = 343 kcal.
copy.s5b: The list below shows the same 30 minutes for every activity, highest first: jumping rope 413, running 343, cycling 280, swimming 203, yoga 88.
copy.s6t: Subtract rest if you want the extra only, then copy
copy.s6b: MET counts the energy you would burn anyway. For the extra from exercise only, subtract about 1 kcal per kg per hour: 35 kcal for 30 minutes at 70 kg. Copy puts the result on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Calories = MET × kg × hours; one MET ≈ 1 kcal per kg per hour at rest.
copy.diagram2: 30 minutes at 70 kg: jumping rope 413, running 343, cycling 280, swimming 203, yoga 88 kcal.

faq.q1: Can I calculate calories burned free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q2: How many calories does 30 minutes of running burn?
faq.a2: About 343 kcal at 10 km/h for a 70 kg person; about 290 at 60 kg.
faq.a3: The energy of an activity compared with sitting still. 1 MET is about 1 kcal per kg per hour.
faq.a4: Within about 20% for most people. Fitness, effort and terrain change the real number.
faq.q5: Where do the values come from?
faq.a5: The 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities by Ainsworth and colleagues.

copy.name: How to calculate compound interest
copy.blurb: Future value = principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years). 1000 at 5% for 10 years grows to 1628.89 compounded yearly, 1647.01 monthly and 1648.66 daily.
copy.title: How to calculate compound interest
copy.lead: You have a deposit or an investment and a yearly rate. You will see what it grows to when interest earns interest, and how often compounding changes the result. 1000 at 5% for 10 years compounded monthly becomes 1647.01, of which 647.01 is interest. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: The future value and the total interest for your principal, rate, years and compounding frequency.
copy.note: Open the compound interest calculator with the principal, the yearly rate and the term at hand. It assumes no deposits or withdrawals along the way and no tax. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: Future value = principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years), where n is how many times a year interest is added. Each period's interest is added to the balance, so the next period earns interest on it too.
copy.s2b: 1000, 5% a year, 10 years and monthly compounding are filled. The future value sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3b: Type the starting amount, the yearly rate in percent and the number of years. Use the nominal rate (APR) the bank quotes, not the effective rate.
copy.s4b: Yearly gives 1628.89, quarterly 1643.62, monthly 1647.01, daily 1648.66. More frequent compounding adds a little each step, with diminishing gains.
copy.s5b: Simple interest would pay 5% of 1000 each year, 500 over 10 years. Compounding adds 147.01 more. The gap widens with higher rates and longer terms.
copy.s6b: The rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ rate. At 5% that is about 14.4 years. Copy puts the future value and interest on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: Future value = principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years).
copy.diagram2: 1000 at 5% for 10 years: yearly 1628.89, monthly 1647.01, daily 1648.66.

faq.q1: Can I calculate compound interest free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.q3: What is the difference from simple interest?
faq.a3: Simple interest pays only on the original amount; compound interest also pays on interest already added.
faq.q4: How long does it take to double?
faq.a4: About 72 ÷ the rate in years: 14.4 years at 5%, 9 years at 8%.
faq.a5: No. It shows one starting amount growing with no deposits, withdrawals or tax.

copy.name: How to remove the background from a photo for free
copy.blurb: Drop JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photos and an AI model cuts out the subject in your browser. Pick transparent, white, a color or blur, then download PNG, WebP or JPG, or all at once as a ZIP.
copy.title: How to remove the background from a photo for free
copy.lead: You have a photo of a person, a product or a pet and want it on a clean background. You will drop the photo, let an AI model cut out the subject in this tab and download the result. Photos never leave your device.
copy.result: A cut-out with a transparent, white, colored or blurred background, downloaded as PNG, WebP or JPG, or several as one ZIP.
copy.note: Open the background remover on a computer or a recent phone. The first run downloads the model once; later runs start at once. Your photos are never uploaded.
copy.s1b: The subject should be in focus and stand out from the background. Hair against a busy background is the hardest case; a plain wall or sky gives the cleanest edge.
copy.s2b: The drop zone accepts JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC. The model runs in this tab on your graphics card when possible, otherwise on the processor.
copy.s3b: Drop one or several photos, or paste one. Each shows Waiting, then Removing background…, then Done. The first run takes longer while the model downloads.
copy.s4b: Hold the image to see the original and compare the outline. Fine hair and transparent objects such as glass may need a second photo against a plainer background.
copy.s5b: Transparent keeps only the subject. White suits product listings and ID-style photos. Color fills any color; Blur keeps the scene softly out of focus behind the subject.
copy.s6b: PNG and WebP keep transparency; JPG gets a white background. Download saves one; Download all (ZIP) saves every finished photo at once.
copy.diagram1: The model runs in your browser: photo in, subject mask out, nothing uploaded.
copy.diagram2: PNG and WebP keep transparency; JPG fills white; ZIP saves every photo.

faq.q1: Can I remove a photo background for free?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs the AI model in your browser at no cost, with no sign-up and no watermark.
faq.a2: No. The model downloads to your browser and the photos stay on your device.
faq.q3: Why is the first run slow?
faq.a3: The model downloads once. Later runs use the cached copy.
faq.a4: PNG and WebP. JPG has no transparency, so it gets a white background.
faq.q5: Can I do several photos at once?
faq.a5: Yes. Drop several and use Download all (ZIP).

copy.name: How to test a regular expression
copy.blurb: Type a pattern, set the g, i, m, s and u flags and paste text to see every match with its capture groups. A replacement such as [$&] or $1 previews the result before you use it in code.
copy.title: How to test a regular expression
copy.lead: You are writing a pattern for code, a search box or a spreadsheet and want to see what it matches before you use it. You will type the pattern, paste sample text and read every match. \b\w+@\w+\.\w+\b finds simple email addresses. Nothing leaves this tab.
copy.result: The number of matches, each match with its position and capture groups, and an optional replace preview, using JavaScript regular expressions.
copy.note: Open the regex tester with a few lines of real text, including lines that should not match. It uses the JavaScript flavour, the same as browsers and Node.js. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s1b: \d is a digit, \w a letter, digit or underscore, \s a space, . any character. + means one or more, * zero or more, ? optional. ( ) captures a group; \b is a word boundary.
copy.s2b: The pattern box, the flags and the test text are ready. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.s3t: Type the pattern and paste text
copy.s3b: Type the pattern without slashes, for example \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} for dates such as 2026-10-29. Paste text with lines that should and should not match.
copy.s4b: g finds every match instead of the first; i ignores case; m makes ^ and $ work per line; s lets . match line breaks; u enables full Unicode. The match count line shows the active flags.
copy.s5b: Each match lists its text and capture groups. (\d{4})-(\d{2}) on 2026-10 gives group 1 = 2026 and group 2 = 10. A pattern that matches too much usually needs \b or a narrower class.
copy.s6b: Type a replacement: $& is the whole match, $1 the first group. [$&] wraps each match in brackets. Copy matches puts every match on the clipboard.
copy.diagram1: \d digit, \w word character, \s space, + one or more, ( ) capture group, \b word boundary.
copy.diagram2: Flags: g all matches, i ignore case, m per line, s dot matches newline, u Unicode.

faq.q1: Can I test a regex free online?
faq.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.a2: JavaScript, the same as browsers and Node.js. Most simple patterns work the same in Python and Java.
faq.q3: Why do I only get one match?
faq.a3: Turn on the g flag to find every match.
faq.q4: How do I use a capture group in the replacement?
faq.a4: $1 is the first group, $2 the second, $& the whole match.
faq.a5: No. Type only the pattern; flags are checkboxes.
